course.title: Snacks and Small Chops
course.tagline: Make samosas, spring rolls, puff puff and small chops for parties and sales.

days.title: What Are Small Chops?
days.goal: Know what small chops are and why people love them.

video.title: Learn Small Chops (Complete Package in 14 mins): Samosa, Spring Roll, and Puff Puff

steps: Small chops are small snacks served at parties and events.
Common ones: samosa, spring roll, puff puff, meat pie, and gizdodo.
They are bite-size, so guests can eat them while standing and talking.
They are fried or baked, and served hot or warm.
Good small chops are crisp outside and tasty inside.
days.task: List five small chops you know.
days.challenge: Taste a small chop and note what makes it good.

quiz.explain: Small chops are bite-size snacks served at events.

options: So guests can eat them while standing and talking
quiz.explain: Bite-size snacks are easy to eat at a party.

quiz.q: What makes a good small chop?
quiz.explain: A good small chop is crisp outside and tasty inside.

days.title: Puff Puff: The Party Favourite
days.goal: Make puff puff, the sweet fried dough balls.

video.title: Nigerian Puff Puff Recipe: How to Make Puff Puff

steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, salt, and warm water into a thick batter.
Cover and leave for 1 hour until it rises and bubbles.
Heat oil in a deep pot. Test with a drop of batter: it should rise at once.
Drop spoonfuls of batter into the oil. Turn them until golden all over.
Drain on paper and serve warm.
days.task: Make a batch of puff puff.
days.challenge: Try a second batch with a little nutmeg and compare.

quiz.q: How thick should puff puff batter be?
options: Thick, so it holds its shape on a spoon
quiz.explain: Thick batter holds its shape and fries into round balls.

quiz.q: How do you know the oil is hot enough?
options: A drop of batter rises at once
quiz.explain: Batter that rises at once means the oil is ready.

quiz.q: Why turn puff puff while frying?
options: So it browns evenly all over
quiz.explain: Turning gives an even golden colour on all sides.

days.title: Samosa: Fold It Right
days.goal: Make samosas with a tasty filling.

video.title: You'll Never Need Another Puff Puff Recipe Again | Street Snacks Ep. 17

steps: Make the filling: fry minced meat with onion, carrot, and peas.
Season well and let the filling cool.
Cut pastry sheets into strips.
Fold each strip into a triangle pocket. Fill and seal the edge with water.
Fry in hot oil until golden and crisp.
days.task: Make a batch of samosas.
days.challenge: Make a second batch with a vegetable filling.

quiz.q: Why must samosa filling be cool?
options: Hot filling makes the pastry soggy
quiz.explain: Hot filling softens the pastry before it fries.

quiz.q: How do you seal a samosa?
quiz.explain: A little water on the edge sticks the pastry closed.

options: Triangles hold filling well and fry evenly
quiz.explain: A triangle pocket holds the filling and fries crisp.

days.title: Spring Rolls: Crisp and Light
days.goal: Make spring rolls from scratch.

video.title: Puff Puff (West African Doughnuts)

steps: Make the filling: fry vegetables and a little meat with seasoning.
Let the filling cool. Wet filling makes rolls soggy.
Place filling on a wrapper. Fold the sides in, then roll tightly.
Seal the edge with a little water or flour paste.
Fry in hot oil until golden and crisp.
days.task: Make a batch of spring rolls.
days.challenge: Make the wrappers from scratch if you have time.

quiz.q: Why must spring roll filling be cool?
options: Wet, hot filling makes rolls soggy
quiz.explain: Cool, dry filling keeps rolls crisp.

options: So they do not open in the oil
quiz.explain: A loose roll opens in hot oil and the filling spills out.

options: Water or flour paste on the edge
quiz.explain: Water or flour paste sticks the edge closed.

days.title: Meat Pie: Flaky and Tasty
days.goal: Make Nigerian meat pie.

video.title: 10 Minutes Snack! Easy Flaky Meat Pie with Puff Pastry

steps: Make the filling: fry minced meat with onion, carrot, and potato.
Season well and let the filling cool.
Make pastry: rub butter into flour until it looks like crumbs.
Add cold water a little at a time until it forms a dough.
Roll out, cut circles, fill, fold, seal, and bake until golden.
days.task: Bake a batch of meat pies.
days.challenge: Make a second batch with chicken filling.

quiz.q: Why must meat pie filling be cool?
quiz.explain: Hot filling melts the butter in the pastry and makes it soggy.

quiz.q: What does rubbing butter into flour do?
quiz.explain: Butter mixed into flour in crumbs makes a flaky crust.

quiz.q: Why use cold water for pastry?
options: Cold water keeps the butter solid so the pastry stays flaky
quiz.explain: Warm water melts the butter and ruins the flaky layers.

days.title: Gizdodo: Plantain and Gizzard
days.goal: Make gizdodo, the party favourite.

video.title: Crispy Samosa & Spring Rolls Recipe (Using the Same Wrap)

steps: Boil gizzard with onion and seasoning until tender.
Cut gizzard into small pieces and fry until crisp.
Fry ripe plantain cubes until golden.
Fry a pepper mix until the oil separates.
Mix plantain, gizzard, and pepper together. Serve hot.
days.task: Make gizdodo.
days.challenge: Serve it on sticks as a party snack.

options: Fried plantain and gizzard mixed in pepper sauce
quiz.explain: Gizdodo is fried plantain and gizzard tossed in pepper sauce.

options: Gizzard is tough and needs boiling to soften
quiz.explain: Gizzard is tough. Boiling softens it before frying.

options: So each part cooks well before mixing
quiz.explain: Plantain and gizzard cook at different speeds, so fry them apart.

days.title: Week 1 Project: A Small Chops Platter
days.goal: Make a platter with four small chops.

video.title: How to Make Spring Rolls from Scratch

steps: Pick four chops: puff puff, samosa, spring roll, and meat pie.
Write a shopping list and costs.
Make fillings first and let them cool.
Fry and bake in order: longest first.
Arrange on a platter and serve to your household.
days.task: Make a platter with four small chops.
days.challenge: Ask everyone which chop they liked best.

options: They need time to cool before they go into pastry
quiz.explain: Fillings must be cool, or they make pastry soggy.

quiz.q: What order do you fry and bake in?
options: Longest first, so all finish together
quiz.explain: Start with what takes longest so all chops are ready together.

quiz.q: Why arrange chops on a platter?
options: A neat platter looks professional and inviting
quiz.explain: A neat platter makes small chops look worth buying.

project.title: Make a Small Chops Platter
project.brief: Make puff puff, samosa, spring roll, and meat pie on one platter.

days.title: Puff Pastry Snacks: Quick and Flaky
days.goal: Make quick snacks with puff pastry.

video.title: How to Make Vegetable Spring Rolls Filling and Wrappers

steps: Buy ready-made puff pastry or make a simple version.
Keep it cold. Warm pastry sticks and will not puff.
Cut into squares. Add minced meat or cheese.
Fold and press the edges with a fork to seal.
Bake at 200°C until puffed up and golden.
days.task: Make puff pastry meat snacks.
days.challenge: Make a sweet version with jam and compare.

quiz.q: Why must puff pastry stay cold?
options: Warm pastry sticks and will not puff up
quiz.explain: Cold butter in the pastry turns to steam and lifts the layers.
Butter between the layers turns to steam and pushes them apart.

quiz.q: Why seal edges with a fork?
options: So the filling does not leak out
quiz.explain: Sealed edges keep the filling inside while it bakes.

days.title: Peppered Chicken and Fish
days.goal: Make peppered chicken and fish for parties.

video.title: Dodo Gizzard / Gizdodo Recipe

steps: Grill or fry your protein first until cooked.
Fry a thick pepper mix with onion until the oil separates.
Add the protein and toss so every piece is coated.
Cook on low for 5 minutes so the pepper sticks.
Serve hot as small chops.
days.task: Make peppered chicken.
days.challenge: Make peppered fish and note how the time differs.

options: So the pepper coats cooked meat instead of stewing raw meat
quiz.explain: Pre-cooked protein takes the pepper sauce without overcooking.

quiz.q: What makes a pepper mix thick enough to coat?
options: Frying it down until most water is gone
quiz.explain: A well-fried, thick pepper mix clings to meat.

quiz.q: What is peppered meat often served as?
quiz.explain: Peppered chicken and fish are classic party small chops.

days.title: Doughnuts: Sweet Party Snacks
days.goal: Make doughnuts for parties.

video.title: How to Make Dodo Gizzard on Stick

steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, milk, butter, and egg into a soft dough.
Let it rise for 1 hour. Roll out and cut rings.
Let the rings rise again for 30 minutes.
Fry in hot oil for 1 minute each side until golden.
Dip in a simple glaze of icing sugar and milk.
days.task: Make a batch of doughnuts.
days.challenge: Try a second batch with a chocolate glaze.

quiz.q: Why let doughnut rings rise a second time?
options: A second rise makes them light and fluffy
quiz.explain: The second rise fills the rings with air so they fry up light.
Doughnuts are small and fry fast, about 1 minute per side.

options: Icing sugar mixed with a little milk
quiz.explain: Icing sugar and a little milk make a simple sweet glaze.

days.title: Buns and Small Breads
days.goal: Make small buns for parties.

video.title: How to Make Flaky Nigerian Meatpie

steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, milk, and butter into a soft dough.
Knead for 10 minutes until smooth.
Let it rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Shape into small balls and bake at 180°C until golden.
Brush with butter while warm.
days.task: Bake a batch of small buns.
days.challenge: Fill half the buns with jam before baking.

options: To build stretch so the buns rise well
quiz.explain: Kneading builds stretch in the dough so buns rise and hold shape.

quiz.q: Why brush buns with butter after baking?
options: To make them last longer only
quiz.explain: Butter on warm buns adds shine and a rich taste.
Buns rise for about 1 hour until doubled in size.

days.title: Sausage Rolls and Mini Pies
days.goal: Make sausage rolls and mini pies.

video.title: How to Make Nigerian Meatpie Like a Pro

steps: Wrap sausage meat in pastry and cut into small rolls.
For mini pies, use the meat pie method but smaller.
Brush the tops with beaten egg for a golden finish.
Bake at 200°C until golden and crisp.
Cool slightly before serving.
days.task: Make a batch of sausage rolls.
days.challenge: Make a batch of mini pies.

options: It gives a golden, shiny finish
quiz.explain: Beaten egg on pastry turns golden and shiny in the oven.
Small rolls are the right size for party snacks.
Fresh-baked filling is very hot. A short rest makes it safe to eat.

days.title: Frying Skills: Oil, Heat, and Safety
days.goal: Fry small chops safely and well.

video.title: Quarantine Cooking: African Doughnuts

steps: Use a deep pot with enough oil to cover the food.
Heat oil until a drop of batter rises at once.
Do not crowd the pot. Fry in batches.
Turn food so it browns evenly.
Drain on paper. Never leave hot oil alone.
days.task: Fry a batch of small chops using safe frying steps.
days.challenge: Fry a second batch without crowding and compare.

quiz.q: How do you know oil is hot enough?
options: A drop of batter rises at once
quiz.explain: Batter that rises at once means the oil is ready.

options: The oil cools down and food goes soggy
quiz.explain: Crowding drops the oil temperature, so food goes soggy.

quiz.q: Why never leave hot oil alone?
quiz.explain: Hot oil left alone can overheat and catch fire.

days.title: Week 2 Project: A Party Box
days.goal: Make a party box with six small chops.

video.title: Puff Pastry and Minced Meat Appetizer with a Trick That Few People Know!

steps: Pick six chops: puff puff, samosa, spring roll, meat pie, gizdodo, and doughnut.
Write a shopping list and costs.
Make fillings first and let them cool.
Fry and bake in order, longest first.
Pack the box neatly and price it.
days.task: Make a party box with six small chops.
days.challenge: Price the box as if you were selling it.

options: Variety makes a party box exciting
quiz.explain: Six different chops give guests lots of choice.
Fillings must be cool, or they make pastry soggy.

options: It teaches you the real cost of your work
quiz.explain: Pricing turns cooking into a business skill.

project.brief: Make six different small chops and pack them as one party box.
checks: Box priced as if for sale

days.title: Costing Small Chops
days.goal: Work out what small chops cost and what to charge.

video.title: Minced Meat Puff Pastry So Tasty That Everyone Will Ask for the Recipe!

steps: List every ingredient with its price.
Add gas, oil, and packaging costs.
Divide the total by the number of pieces you made.
Charge 2 to 3 times the cost per piece for a profit.
Compare with small chops sellers near you.
days.task: Cost a batch of puff puff and set a price per piece.
days.challenge: Cost a batch of samosas the same way.

quiz.q: What is the cost per piece?
options: Total cost divided by the number of pieces
quiz.explain: Cost per piece is the total cost shared across all the pieces you made.

quiz.q: Why charge 2 to 3 times the cost?
options: To cover gas, oil, packaging, and your time, and still make a profit
quiz.explain: The extra covers all the costs beyond ingredients and leaves profit.

quiz.q: What else must you add to the cost?
quiz.explain: Gas, oil, and packaging are real costs of every chop.

days.title: Packing Small Chops for Delivery
days.goal: Pack small chops so they stay crisp.

video.title: I Stopped Rolling Dough — Now I Bake Dinner Pies This Way

steps: Let chops cool slightly before packing. Hot chops make steam.
Use boxes with paper inside to soak up oil.
Do not pack hot chops in sealed plastic. They go soggy.
Label with the contents and the date.
Deliver fast. Small chops are best fresh.
days.task: Pack a box of small chops as if for delivery.
days.challenge: Deliver a box to someone and ask for feedback.

quiz.q: Why cool chops slightly before packing?
options: Hot chops make steam and go soggy
quiz.explain: Steam in a closed box makes crisp chops soft.

quiz.q: Why use paper in the box?
options: Paper soaks up oil and keeps chops crisp
quiz.explain: Paper soaks up extra oil so chops stay crisp.
Small chops go soft over time, so fast delivery matters.

days.title: Small Chops for Weddings
days.goal: Plan small chops for a wedding.

video.title: Learn Small Chops (Complete Package in 14 mins): Samosa, Spring Roll, and Puff Puff

steps: Ask how many guests and what chops they want.
Plan 4 to 5 pieces per guest.
Make fillings in advance. Fry on the day.
Hire a helper if the order is big.
Pack in boxes and deliver on time.
days.task: Plan small chops for a wedding of 100 guests on paper.
days.challenge: Work out the amounts and costs.

quiz.q: How many small chops per guest?
quiz.explain: Four to five pieces per guest is a good guide.

options: Fried chops go soft if made early
quiz.explain: Fried chops are best fresh. Fry them on the day.

quiz.q: Why hire a helper for big orders?
options: So the work gets done on time
quiz.explain: A helper keeps big orders on schedule.

days.title: Taking Small Chops Orders
days.goal: Take a small chops order like a professional.

video.title: Nigerian Puff Puff Recipe: How to Make Puff Puff

steps: Ask the date, the number of guests, and the chops wanted.
Ask about allergies. Write them down.
Write a quote with the price per box and the total.
Take a deposit to book the date.
Confirm everything in writing a few days before.
days.task: Practise taking an order from a friend.
days.challenge: Write an order form you can use for real customers.

options: Money paid in advance to book the date
quiz.explain: A deposit books the date and covers your costs if the customer cancels.

options: So you do not cook food that could harm someone
quiz.explain: Allergies can be serious. Always ask and write the answer down.
A written confirmation stops mistakes about date, numbers, and menu.

days.title: Small Chops Business: First Steps
days.goal: Take your first steps toward selling small chops.

video.title: You'll Never Need Another Puff Puff Recipe Again | Street Snacks Ep. 17

Set your prices from your costing work.
Take clear photos of your chops in good light.
Tell friends and family first. Ask them to share.
Take orders in advance so you cook only what is sold.
days.task: Take photos of your best small chops and show them to three people.
days.challenge: Take one real order, even a small one, and deliver it on time.

quiz.q: Why start with only 3 or 4 chops?
options: A small menu is easier to make well and cost
quiz.explain: A small menu keeps quality high and costing simple.

options: So you cook only what is sold and waste nothing
quiz.explain: Advance orders mean no waste and no guessing.

options: Clear photos help people decide to buy
quiz.explain: People buy with their eyes first. Good photos sell chops.

days.title: Small Chops Mistakes and Fixes
days.goal: Fix the commonest small chops problems.

video.title: Puff Puff (West African Doughnuts)

steps: Chops went soggy? Oil was not hot enough, or you packed them too soon.
Samosas opened in the oil? Seal edges well with water.
Pastry is hard? You over-mixed the dough or used warm water.
Filling is dry? Add a little oil or stock to the filling.
Write down each problem and fix.
days.task: Fix one small chops problem you have had.
days.challenge: Write a list of three problems and how you would fix them.

options: Oil was not hot enough, or they were packed too soon
quiz.explain: Cool oil and packing too soon make chops soggy.

quiz.q: Why did samosas open in the oil?
quiz.explain: Loose edges open in hot oil. Seal them well with water.
Over-mixing and warm water make pastry tough.

days.task: Cater small chops for a party of 20 or more.
days.challenge: Work out your sales, costs, and profit.

steps: Offer light chops in hot weather and hearty chops in cold weather.
Add one new chop each season.
Ask customers what they want next.

quiz.q: Why drop chops that do not sell?

quiz.explain: Written orders stop mistakes and show what sells.

days.challenge: Write a food safety list for your business.

quiz.q: Why fry food until cooked through?
